blocks.text: Sourcing Manager — B.FTech in Apparel Production Technology

blocks.label: Career category
blocks.text: Manufacturing & Industrial Production
QUALIFICATION
B.FTech / Fashion-related degree
Apparel Production Technology
CAREER LEVEL
Early to senior career
Sourcing coordination to supplier and sourcing leadership
A Sourcing Manager identifies, evaluates, negotiates with, and manages suppliers to obtain the right materials or finished products at the required cost, quality, quantity, and delivery schedule.

In the apparel industry, sourcing can involve fabrics, yarns, trims, accessories, packaging, garment manufacturers, and finished apparel. The manager coordinates with merchandising, product development, production, quality, logistics, finance, and suppliers to ensure sourcing decisions support business objectives.
This role is suitable for students interested in apparel and textiles, negotiation, supplier relationships, cost analysis, international trade, and supply-chain management.
Typical responsibilities

items.text: Identify and assess fabric mills, garment factories, trim suppliers, and other vendors.
Compare quotations, quality, lead times, production capacity, and commercial terms.
Negotiate pricing, minimum order quantities, payment terms, and delivery schedules.
Track material availability and supplier performance.
Coordinate sample development, approvals, purchase orders, and order fulfilment.
Monitor supplier risks, delays, quality problems, and cost fluctuations.
Support ethical sourcing, traceability, and applicable buyer or regulatory requirements.
Build long-term supplier relationships while maintaining cost and quality targets.

blocks.text: B.FTech — Apparel Production Technology
Learn textiles, garment manufacturing, costing, and supply chains
Sourcing / Purchase Trainee
Support supplier research, quotations, samples, and purchase orders
Sourcing Executive / Buyer
Manage categories, suppliers, costs, and delivery follow-ups
Sourcing Manager
Own sourcing strategy, supplier performance, negotiations, and risk
Head of Sourcing / Supply Chain Director
Lead sourcing strategy, teams, budgets, and supplier networks

The exact progression varies by employer and sourcing specialisation. Graduates generally begin in trainee, coordinator, assistant buyer, or executive positions before taking responsibility for sourcing strategy and teams.
Year 1 — Apparel and textile foundations
Academic focus

items.text: Textile fibres, yarns, fabrics, and fabric properties.
Apparel construction, garment components, seams, and stitches.
Introduction to garment manufacturing processes.
Basic mathematics, statistics, and business communication.
Fundamentals of costing and computer applications.

blocks.text: Practical skills

items.text: Identify common apparel fabrics and trims.
Understand the difference between raw materials, components, and finished goods.
Learn how garment construction affects material choices and product cost.
Practise professional emails, supplier enquiries, and spreadsheet organisation.

blocks.label: Suggested mini-project
blocks.text: Create a sourcing specification sheet for a basic T-shirt, listing fabric composition, GSM, colour, trims, quality requirements, and packaging needs.
Year 2 — Procurement, costing, and supplier evaluation
Academic focus

items.text: Apparel merchandising and sourcing processes.
Fabric and garment costing.
Supplier identification and evaluation.
Quality assurance and material inspection.
Inventory management and purchasing fundamentals.
Production planning and delivery lead times.

blocks.text: Practical skills

items.text: Compare supplier quotations using a standard template.
Calculate basic material consumption and estimated costs.
Understand minimum order quantities, sample approvals, and lead times.
Maintain a supplier database and purchase-order tracker.
Identify how fabric quality and availability affect production.

blocks.label: Suggested mini-project
blocks.text: Compare three hypothetical fabric suppliers using price, quality, lead time, minimum order quantity, and reliability criteria.
Year 3 — Strategic sourcing and supply-chain management
Academic focus

items.text: Strategic sourcing and supplier relationship management.
Negotiation and commercial contract fundamentals.
Supply-chain risk and inventory planning.
International trade, logistics, and trade documentation.
Sustainable sourcing, traceability, and ethical supply chains.
Data analysis for procurement and sourcing decisions.

blocks.text: Practical skills

items.text: Prepare a supplier scorecard.
Evaluate the total cost of sourcing rather than price alone.
Track order status, material delays, and supplier performance.
Analyse the causes of sourcing delays and cost variations.
Develop alternative-supplier plans for critical materials.

blocks.label: Suggested mini-project
blocks.text: Build a sourcing dashboard showing supplier prices, lead times, defect rates, on-time delivery, and risk ratings.
Year 4 — Strategic application and industry readiness
If the programme is four years long, use this stage for advanced electives, industrial training, and a capstone project.
Focus areas

items.text: Category sourcing strategy and supplier portfolio management.
Cost modelling, negotiation preparation, and budget control.
Vendor audits, compliance documentation, and risk assessment.
Global sourcing, logistics coordination, and delivery planning.
Procurement analytics and digital supply-chain systems.

blocks.label: Capstone project
blocks.text: Develop a sourcing strategy for a small apparel collection. Include material specifications, supplier comparison, estimated costs, lead times, quality requirements, risk analysis, and a sourcing recommendation.
Industry preparation

items.text: Complete an internship in sourcing, merchandising, procurement, or supply-chain operations.
Practise supplier evaluation and quotation comparison using simulated or authorised data.
Prepare a portfolio of sourcing reports and dashboards.
Learn to justify supplier choices with commercial and operational evidence.

blocks.text: Supplier management and negotiation
Supplier research, quotation comparison, negotiation, relationship management, performance reviews, and conflict resolution.
Costing and commercial analysis
Material costing, price benchmarking, total cost of ownership, budget tracking, minimum order quantities, and commercial terms.
Apparel and material knowledge
Fabric properties, garment construction, trims, material specifications, quality requirements, and production lead times.
Planning and risk management
Supplier scorecards, delivery tracking, supply disruption planning, inventory coordination, and data-driven decisions.
Communication and collaboration
Professional email writing, documentation, cross-functional coordination, presentation, and stakeholder management.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Supplier comparison matrix
Compare three hypothetical fabric suppliers by price, quality, lead time, minimum order quantity, payment terms, and reliability.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Excel scorecard and documented supplier recommendation.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Apparel sourcing cost model
Estimate fabric and trim requirements, unit material cost, freight, and other relevant sourcing costs.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Costing workbook with clearly stated assumptions.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Supplier performance dashboard
Analyse on-time delivery, defect rates, lead times, and cost changes using simulated or authorised data.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Excel or Power BI dashboard.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Sourcing risk assessment
Assess risks such as supplier concentration, delayed materials, quality failures, and price volatility.

blocks.label: Deliverable
blocks.text: Risk register with mitigation actions and alternative-supplier plans.

blocks.text: Organisations and industry segments to investigate

items.text: Apparel exporters and garment manufacturers.
Textile mills, fabric suppliers, and trim manufacturers.
Fashion retailers and apparel brands with sourcing or buying teams.
Buying houses and sourcing agencies.
Supply-chain, procurement, and logistics service providers.

blocks.text: Examples of apparel and textile businesses to research include Arvind, Gokaldas Exports, and Shahi Exports, along with fashion retailers and buying houses. These are examples to investigate, not confirmed current vacancies. Check official career pages and college placement channels.
What to learn during an internship

items.text: How sourcing specifications and supplier quotations are prepared.
How samples and materials are approved.
How price, quality, quantity, and delivery terms are evaluated.
How purchase orders and supplier follow-ups are managed.
How sourcing teams resolve delays, quality issues, and material shortages.

blocks.text: Prioritise courses that develop practical sourcing and procurement skills.

rows.text: Apparel merchandising
Product specifications, material sourcing, costing, and buyer requirements
Procurement and sourcing
Supplier selection, purchasing processes, negotiation, and contracts
Supply-chain management
Inventory, logistics, lead times, and supply-chain risk
Data analysis
Excel, Power BI, and basic statistical analysis
Quality management
Supplier quality, inspection, corrective action, and performance monitoring
Sustainability and compliance
Responsible sourcing, traceability, and relevant supplier standards

blocks.text: Explore relevant training from recognised textile and apparel institutes, professional procurement bodies, and established online learning providers. Verify course recognition, fees, prerequisites, and current availability before enrolling.
Further study can support progression into strategic sourcing, procurement leadership, or broader supply-chain management.

blocks.label: M.FTech in Apparel Production
blocks.text: Useful for deeper understanding of apparel manufacturing and material requirements.

items.text: MBA in Operations or Supply Chain Management: Relevant for procurement strategy, supplier networks, and operations leadership.
Postgraduate programme in International Business: Can support work involving global suppliers and international trade.
Specialised procurement or sourcing qualifications: Useful for structured learning in supplier management, contracts, and procurement processes.

blocks.text: A postgraduate degree is not mandatory for every sourcing role. Practical experience, negotiation ability, commercial judgement, and industry knowledge are also important.

Reset checklist
By graduation, a career-ready candidate should be able to demonstrate:

items.text: Strong fundamentals in apparel production, fabrics, trims, and material specifications.
The ability to compare suppliers on cost, quality, capacity, and delivery.
Basic knowledge of sourcing, procurement, purchase orders, and inventory.
Practical Excel skills and familiarity with sourcing analytics.
An understanding of supplier risk, ethical sourcing, and material traceability.
At least one sourcing-related project and, where possible, relevant industry experience.
Professional communication, negotiation preparation, and cross-functional coordination.

blocks.label: Recommended first target
blocks.text: Aim for a Sourcing Trainee, Sourcing Coordinator, Procurement Assistant, or Apparel Merchandising Assistant role. Build experience in supplier evaluation, costing, and order execution before progressing toward a Sourcing Manager position.
